title: Your neighbor
hookLine: faith lived beside neighbors of every kind

lines: AS IF THE NEIGHBOR WERE AN HEIR.
cards: The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, once told his companions: Jibril kept urging me to treat the neighbor well, so often that I thought he was going to make the neighbor an heir. That report is in Sahih al-Bukhari.
An heir. Someone with a share in what is yours, written into the family accounts. The person whose music comes through the wall, whose car blocks yours, whose name you might not even know.
You met the neighbor back on day one hundred fifty-four. Today, faith lived beside neighbors of every kind.

teach.h: THE NEAR NEIGHBOR AND THE STRANGER.
teach.b: In surah an-Nisa, in a list of those to be treated with kindness, after parents, relatives, orphans and the needy, the Qur'an names the neighbor who is related to you, the neighbor who is a stranger, and the companion at your side.
Two kinds of neighbor in one verse: one who shares your family, and one who shares nothing with you but a fence. The bar is set high.

In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor. And in the same collection, that a person whose neighbor isn't safe from his harm will not enter paradise.
So a neighbor isn't a matter of manners. It sits right next to faith itself. Neighbors of every kind, too.

teach.h: HAVE YOU GIVEN SOME NEXT DOOR?
teach.b: A report in the collections of Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi tells of the companion Abdullah ibn Amr, who had a sheep slaughtered at home and asked his household: have you given some to our Jewish neighbor?
Then he repeated the hadith of Jibril and the neighbor. The neighbor's faith didn't change the neighbor's right. On an ordinary street it starts small.
Knowing a name. Not letting your trash cans block a driveway. Keeping the noise down at night.
A plate of food over the fence on a holiday, any holiday. Checking on the older man upstairs when it snows.
Rights like these are small, and they're owed whether or not the neighbor returns them.

how: Muslims treat the neighbor's rights as part of faith, following the Qur'an's command to be kind to the near and the stranger neighbor and the hadith 'let him honor his neighbor'; this can mean sharing food on holidays, avoiding noise and harm, and checking on neighbors of any faith.

o: a close relative who lives with you in the family home
the one through the wall, whose rights sit right next to faith
only a fellow Muslim who lives on the same street as you

p: kept urging kindness to the neighbor
the near neighbor and the stranger
sent meat to his Jewish neighbor
whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day

s: in Islam, a neighbor's rights depend on their religion
Abdullah ibn Amr made sure his Jewish neighbor got a share of the meat, and repeated the hadith of Jibril.
the Prophet said he thought Jibril would make the neighbor an heir
Jibril kept urging him about the neighbor until he thought so (Sahih al-Bukhari).
treating a neighbor well is only about good manners
the hadith ties it to faith: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor.

games.q: you're Abdullah ibn Amr. a sheep has been slaughtered at your house and the meat is being shared out. what do you ask your household?
o: have you given some to our Jewish neighbor?
have you kept enough for us?
have you sent it all to the mosque?
games.why: he asked whether they had given some to their Jewish neighbor, and repeated the Prophet's words about Jibril urging care for the neighbor (Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi).

practice: In your mind, step out your front door and look left, right, up or down, silently naming every neighbor whose name you know, and notice where the names run out.

Pick one door where you don't know a name, and let one small, easy reason to knock come to mind: an introduction, a plate of something, a question about the building. If you pray, ask Allah to bless the people on your street.

wordCard.voice: Your neighbor. The person on the other side of the wall, whose rights the Qur'an and the Prophet set right next to faith. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: start next door. A name is where it begins. Back tomorrow, same hill.
